about.ai_body: Home-page tips are computed on your computer from your own data and plan. The optional AI uses Ollama on this machine only (127.0.0.1); it is told never to recommend buying or selling.
about.disclaimer: Maze Crypto is an information tool. It does not give investment, financial or tax advice, and nothing it shows — prices, indicators, alerts, allocations — is a recommendation to buy or sell. Data can be delayed or wrong. You alone are responsible for your decisions.
about.keys_body: Private keys, seed phrases, exchange API keys and passwords. If anything claiming to be Maze Crypto asks for one, it is not this app.
about.privacy_body: No telemetry, no accounts. The app only connects to the hosts listed below and refuses any other. With the proxy option on, every request — including DNS — goes through Tor or your SOCKS5 proxy. Your trades stay in a local SQLite file.
about.title: About
about.what_body: Tracks prices from public market data, keeps your manually entered trades, computes average cost and profit/loss, follows a recurring-buy plan and notifies you when rules you defined become true. It never places orders.

chart.g.average_b: Smooth out the noise. When the price stays above them, the trend is up; below them, down.
chart.g.candles_b: Each candle is one period. Green: closed higher than it opened. Red: closed lower. The thin lines show the highest and lowest price.
chart.g.levels_b: Dashed orange lines you draw yourself (Add level, or Ctrl+click) to mark prices you care about.
chart.g.macd_b: Fast minus slow average. Bars above zero: momentum up; below zero: momentum down.
chart.g.rsi_b: A 0–100 gauge of how fast the price moved recently. Above 70: fast rise. Below 30: fast fall.
chart.g.title: How to read this chart
chart.g.volume_b: The bars at the bottom: how much was traded. A move on high volume is more significant.
chart.help.ema21: Average of the last 21 candles, weighted toward recent ones: reacts faster.
chart.help.macd: Difference between a fast and a slow average; above its signal line, momentum is rising.
chart.help.rsi: Relative Strength Index (0–100). Above 70: rose fast. Below 30: fell fast.
chart.help.sma200: Average of the last 200 candles: the long-term trend.
chart.help.sma50: Average closing price of the last 50 candles. Price above it = recent trend up.
chart.help.vol: How much was traded in each candle. Big moves on high volume carry more weight.
chart.iv_tip: Candle size: each candle covers 1 hour, 4 hours, 1 day or 1 week
chart.level_line_tip: Drag to move · double-click to delete
chart.level_tip: Add a support/resistance line at the last price. Ctrl+click on the chart adds one anywhere.
chart.title: Chart
chart.x.cost_above: The price is {pct}% above your average price of {avg} (dashed line on the chart).
chart.x.cost_below: The price is {pct}% below your average price of {avg} (dashed line on the chart).
chart.x.long_down: The 50-period average is below the 200-period one: the longer trend is down.
chart.x.long_up: The 50-period average is above the 200-period one: the longer trend is up too.
chart.x.macd_b: Based on MACD versus its signal line.
chart.x.note: Describes the past and present only. Not a forecast, not advice.
chart.x.rsi_calm_b: Between 30 and 70: recent gains and losses are roughly balanced.
chart.x.rsi_cold_b: {coin} has fallen fast. That describes the recent past; it does not say what comes next.
chart.x.rsi_hot_b: {coin} has risen fast. Such stretches often cool down for a while — a description, not a forecast.
chart.x.title: What the chart says
chart.x.trend_down_b: The price is below its 50-period average, so the recent direction has been down.
chart.x.trend_up_b: The price is above its 50-period average, so the recent direction has been up.
chart.your_avg_tip: The average price you paid, from your purchases.
col.ath_tip: How far the price is below its all-time high (ATH).
col.corr_tip: How closely the coin moved with Bitcoin over 30 days. 1 = in lockstep, 0 = unrelated.
col.mcap_tip: Market capitalisation: price × coins in circulation.

dca.empty: No plan yet. A plan splits a fixed amount across coins every week, two weeks or month.

dca.log_trades: Also record these purchases as trades

dcaed.extras_help: Extra purchases added to a single period, e.g. a reserve buy in period 1.
dcaed.follow: Split each period toward my target allocation
dcaed.follow_note: Each period is split to move the portfolio toward its targets.

hold.no_targets: No target allocation yet — set one with Targets.
hold.split_note: Shows how a new contribution would move the portfolio toward its targets without selling. Arithmetic only, not a recommendation.

ins.avg_corr_sub: How much your watchlist moves together (30 days)
ins.corr_note: 1.00 = move together, 0 = unrelated, negative = opposite. Highly correlated coins diversify each other less.
ins.disclaimer: These figures describe the past and present; they do not predict prices and are not advice.
ins.g.corr_b: 1.00 = two coins move together, 0 = unrelated, negative = opposite. The brighter the cell, the closer they move.
ins.g.dd_b: The largest drop from a high to a later low within the last 90 days.
ins.g.macd_b: Above its signal line: momentum rising. Below: slowing.
ins.g.rsi_b: 0–100. Above 70: the price rose fast recently; below 30: it fell fast.
ins.g.title: What these mean
ins.g.trend_b: Where the price is compared with its 50- and 200-day averages.
ins.g.vol_b: How much the price swings, per year. Higher means bigger ups and downs.
ins.stable_sub: of your portfolio is in stablecoins
ins.sub: The state of your coins and portfolio, in numbers and in words
ins.tech_help: Each coin's daily chart summed up. Hover a column title for what it means.
ins.title: Insights
learn.ath.b: ATH is the highest price ever paid. The “from peak” column shows how far below it each coin is today.
learn.avg_cost.b: Your average cost is everything you paid (fees included) divided by the coins you hold. You are in profit when the price is above it.
learn.correlation.b: Many altcoins move with Bitcoin. Owning several coins that move together spreads your money less than it seems.
learn.dca.b: Buying a fixed amount on a schedule means you buy more coins when the price is low and fewer when it is high, without having to guess the timing.
learn.drawdown.b: Drawdown is the drop from a peak to a later low. In crypto, drawdowns of 50% or more have happened many times.
learn.fees.b: Every purchase has a fee. Entering it with your purchases keeps your average cost honest.
learn.reserve.b: Stablecoins like USDT or USDC track the US dollar. They do not grow, but they do not swing either.
learn.rsi.b: RSI (0–100) compares recent gains with recent losses. Above 70 the price rose fast, below 30 it fell fast.
learn.targets.b: A target mix (say 50% BTC, 30% ETH, 20% other) turns “what should I buy next?” into simple arithmetic.
learn.volatility.b: Volatility is how much a price swings. A coin with 80% yearly volatility can easily move 5% in a day.

rule.edge_note: A rule notifies when its condition becomes true, then stays quiet until it turns false again and the cooldown has passed.
rule.err_sma: The fast SMA must be shorter than the slow one.
rule.help.cost_change: Negative = below your average cost (−15 = 15% under), positive = above it.
rule.help.drift: True when a target bucket is more than this many percentage points off its target.
rule.help.move: Price change over the last N hours (hourly candles).
rule.help.price: True while the price is at or beyond the level.
rule.help.rsi: Wilder's RSI on the chosen candle interval.
rule.help.sma_cross: Golden: fast SMA crosses above slow. Death: crosses below.
rule.message_ph: Shown in the notification, e.g. your planned step

set.profile_tip: Each profile has its own trades, targets, rules and plan. Type a new name to create one.

tip.balance_ok.b: Every coin is within {pp} points of the share you chose.
tip.below_cost.b: It is {pct}% under your average price of {avg}. This is a paper loss — it only becomes real if you sell.
tip.concentration.b: {coin} is {pct}% of your portfolio, so its price moves your whole portfolio almost one to one.
tip.concentration.t: Most of your money is in one coin
tip.drift.t: Your portfolio has drifted from your targets
tip.drift_over.b: {coin} is {actual}% of your portfolio; your target is {target}% ({pp} points over).
tip.drift_split.b: Following your own targets, your next {amount} would go to: {split}.
tip.drift_under.b: {coin} is {actual}% of your portfolio; your target is {target}% ({pp} points under).
tip.move.b: {coin} moved {pct} in 24 hours. Moves this size are common in crypto; your plan does not have to change because of one day.
tip.near_ath.b: It is only {pct}% below the highest price it ever reached.
tip.no_price.b: {coins}: none of your price sources list it, so its value is missing from the total.
tip.no_rate.b: They have no USD exchange rate, so profit in dollars cannot be calculated. Edit them and add the rate of that day.
tip.no_rate.t: USD profit is unknown for {n} purchases
tip.no_reserve.b: Some people keep part of their crypto in a dollar-pegged coin (e.g. USDT) as a calm reserve for planned purchases.
tip.offline.b: Prices shown are the last ones saved. They update automatically when the connection returns.
tip.plan_soon.t: A planned purchase is coming up
tip.rsi_cold.b: Its RSI is {rsi} (below 30 counts as “stretched” to the downside). This describes recent moves, it does not predict the next one.
tip.rsi_hot.b: Its RSI is {rsi} (above 70 counts as “stretched”). Fast rises often pause for a while — this describes the past, it does not predict.
tip.stale.b: A price source did not answer, so older saved data is shown for it.
tip.start_plan.b: A buying plan (DCA) spreads purchases over weeks or months, so you do not have to pick the right day.
tip.start_rules.b: Alerts send a desktop notification when something you care about happens, e.g. a coin falls 15% below what you paid.

tip.start_targets.b: Set what share of your portfolio each coin should be. The assistant will then tell you when you drift away from it.

wal.title: Wallet
wal.empty_b: Paste the public address of any wallet — Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, Cardano, TON, Dogecoin and 30 more networks. Its balance and transfers are read from the blockchain and your portfolio follows it. Add as many addresses per coin as you like.
wal.safe_b: Only public information is used — addresses, account keys (xpub) and, for Monero, the view key, which can see incoming payments but never spend. The app never asks for, stores or sends a recovery phrase or spending key, and cannot move funds.
wal.privacy_b: To read a balance the address is sent to a public blockchain explorer (Blockstream, Blockscout, Solana, TronGrid, XRPL …), which can link it to your IP address. Turn on the Tor/SOCKS proxy in Settings (expert) to hide it. Addresses stay on this computer.
wal.history_failed: Transfers could not be loaded right now.
wal.history_partial: Some addresses' transfers could not be loaded.
wal.history_note: Values at today's price. Double-click a transfer to open it in a block explorer. Zero-value and unknown-token transfers (often scam bait) are hidden.
wal.no_history_chain: Transfer history is shown for Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Hyperliquid, TRON, Litecoin and XRP addresses. For other networks, open the address in its explorer.
wal.no_history_chain_one: Balances on {chain} are read from a public node; its transfer history is in the explorer.
wal.address_ph: bc1…, 0x…, T…, Solana or Monero address
wal.address_help: Paste a public receiving address. The network is detected and the checksum verified.
wal.address_fixed: The address and network cannot be changed; delete the wallet and add a new one instead.
wal.networks_multi: Networks to check — the same address works on all of them
wal.l2_note: On this network balances (the coin and major stablecoins) are read; transfers open in the explorer.
wal.reference_help: Only for your reference. Never a recovery phrase or private key.
wal.xmr_note: Entered by hand. For a balance that follows the blockchain, add the wallet in the Monero tab with its private view key — it is scanned on this phone, over Tor.
wal.manual_note: A balance you enter yourself — for coins without a public lookup, or coins on an exchange. Update it when it changes.
wal.label: Name (optional)
wal.in_portfolio_help: Off = watch only, e.g. someone else's address.
wal.ignored: {n} other tokens hidden — unknown, without a price or a real market (e.g. airdropped meme tokens), flagged as scam or dust.
wal.indexer_price: Some tokens are priced by the chain's explorer (Blockscout / Jupiter), not CoinGecko.
wal.no_browser: No browser to open the link.
wal.err_stale: Showing the last known balance — update failed: {err}
wal.err_duplicate: This address is already added on {chain}.
wal.delete_b: Only the address is removed from the app. Nothing happens to the funds.
wal.coin_none: No wallet holds this coin yet. Add an address to follow its balance here and in your portfolio.
wal.secret_seed: That looks like a recovery phrase (seed words).
wal.secret_private_key: That looks like a private key.
wal.secret_xprv: That looks like an extended private key (xprv).
wal.secret_b: Anyone who has it can take your funds. It was not saved and has been cleared from the field and the clipboard. Maze Crypto only needs the public receiving address. If you pasted it into any other app or website, move your funds to a new wallet.
wal.bad_xpub: Not a valid extended public key.
wal.bad_testnet: That is a testnet address; only mainnet is supported.
wal.bad_checksum: The checksum does not match — a character is wrong or missing. Copy the address again.
wal.bad_unknown: Not a recognised address. Supported: Bitcoin, Ethereum and EVM networks, Solana, XRP, Cardano, TON, Dogecoin, Bitcoin Cash, Litecoin, TRON, Polkadot, Cosmos, Stellar, NEAR (name.near), Algorand, Tezos, Kaspa, Dash, Zcash (t-address), Hyperliquid, Monero.
wal.bad_not_xmr: That is not a Monero address.
hold.unknown_cost: Profit/loss counts only coins with recorded buys. No buys recorded for: {coins}. Add trades for them to see it.
hold.wallets_only: Amounts come from your wallets. Record your buys under Trades to also see profit and loss.
wal.name: Name
wal.secret_spend_key: That is the private SPEND key of this wallet, not the view key.
wal.valid_account: Valid account key — every address of this account will be watched.
wal.account_b: The account key gives every receiving and change address of the account, so the whole balance is followed — not just one address. It cannot spend. Check that the first address below matches your wallet.
wal.verify_hint: Before receiving a large amount, check the address on your Ledger (Ledger screen → Verify).
ledger.title: Add from Ledger
ledger.cta_b: Read your Ledger accounts over USB or Bluetooth — watch-only.
ledger.safe_b: Maze Crypto only asks your Ledger for public keys. It has no command that signs or sends anything, and your recovery phrase never leaves the device.
ledger.evm_nets: Watch the Ethereum accounts on these networks (same address):
ledger.usb_help: Nano S Plus, Nano X, Stax, Flex over USB.
ledger.ble_help: Nano X, Stax, Flex. Turn Bluetooth on; the first time, confirm the pairing code on the Ledger.
ledger.steps_b: Unlock the Ledger with your PIN. The {app} app must be installed (Ledger Live → My Ledger); the app opens it for you if the device is on the dashboard — confirm on the device.
ledger.look_at_device: Keep the Ledger unlocked and watch its screen.
ledger.verify_on_device: Compare what the Ledger shows with the app, then approve on the device.
ledger.discovery_note: Accounts are found the way Ledger Live does: account 1, 2, 3 … until the first unused one.
ledger.err_locked: The Ledger is locked. Unlock it with your PIN and try again.
ledger.err_wrong_app: Open the {app} app on the Ledger and try again.
ledger.err_not_installed: The {app} app is not installed on this Ledger. Install it with Ledger Live (My Ledger).
ledger.err_no_device: No Ledger found. Check the cable / OTG adapter, or Bluetooth.
ledger.err_permission: USB access was not allowed. Plug the Ledger in again and allow Maze Crypto.
ledger.err_bt_permission: Bluetooth permission is needed to find a Ledger.
ledger.err_scan: Bluetooth search failed. Turn Bluetooth off and on, then try again.
ledger.err_pairing: Pairing did not finish. Confirm the code on the Ledger, or forget the device in Bluetooth settings and pair again.
ledger.err_timeout: The Ledger did not answer in time.
ledger.err_protocol: Unexpected answer from the Ledger. Update its firmware and apps with Ledger Live.
ledger.err_bad_request: The {app} app refused the request. Update it with Ledger Live.
ledger.err_status: The Ledger returned an error. Update the {app} app and try again.
xmr.address_help: The wallet's main address (starts with 4), not a subaddress.
xmr.view_key_help: 64 characters. Feather / Monero GUI: Wallet → Keys. Cake: Wallet keys. It can see incoming payments but cannot spend. Never enter the spend key or the seed.
xmr.restore: Wallet created on (date or block height)
xmr.restore_help: YYYY-MM-DD. Scanning starts there; older payments are not found. Earlier is safer but slower.
xmr.err_restore: Enter the date the wallet was created (YYYY-MM-DD) or a block height.
xmr.key_primary: Use the primary address (starts with 4). A view-only wallet cannot be made from a subaddress or an integrated address.
xmr.key_format: A view key is 64 hexadecimal characters.
xmr.key_mismatch: This view key does not belong to this address.
xmr.tor_b: Monero goes only through the Tor proxy at {host}:{port} (Settings → Tor & Monero) to onion nodes; with Tor off nothing is sent.
xmr.view_b: The view key stays on this computer, in your desktop keyring; nodes only serve the same blocks to everyone. A view key sees incoming payments; spends are recognised by the change they return. A send of the whole balance without change is not seen — then the balance shows too much.
xmr.err_tor_off: Tor is not running. Start Orbot (or check the address in Settings → Tor).
xmr.err_tor_check: Could not confirm the connection goes through Tor.
xmr.err_not_tor: The proxy is not Tor. Monero is only synced over Tor.
xmr.err_node: The Monero node address is not valid.
xmr.err_node_http: A clearnet node must use https:// — or use an .onion node.
xmr.err_no_key: The view key is missing on this phone (backups do not carry it). Remove the wallet and add it again.
tor.title: Tor (Orbot) & Monero
tor.help: Monero always goes through Tor. Maze Linux runs the tor service on 127.0.0.1 : 9050 (Tor Browser uses 9150).
tor.node_help: Empty = Maze's list of community onion nodes. Your own: xyz.onion:18081 or https://host:18089.
ledger.coins_help: Pick as many as you like: one connection reads them all. The app opens each coin's app on the Ledger in turn — you only confirm "open" on the device.
ledger.xmr_help: Monero: the date your Ledger Monero wallet was first used (YYYY-MM-DD). Scanning starts there.
ledger.steps_multi: Plug in and unlock the Ledger. The coin apps must be installed (Ledger Live → My Ledger). The app opens each coin's app in turn — confirm "open" on the device. For Monero the Ledger asks to export the view key: allow it — it can only see incoming payments, never spend.
ledger.err_xmr_view_declined: The view key was not exported (declined on the Ledger), so Monero cannot be watched.
ledger.udev_hint: Plug it in and unlock it. If it is plugged in, install the ledger-udev package (USB access rules) and plug it in again.
xmr.view_key_ph: 64 hexadecimal characters — never the spend key or the seed
xmr.restore_auto: Not needed: recent payments appear first, then the history is read backwards. A date only makes it faster.
xmr.history_so_far: History read back to {date} · {n} payments found. The balance is complete once it reaches the wallet's first payment.
xmr.history_stopped: History read back to {date} ({n} payments) and stopped there.
